91:1: Interpretation of Surat Ash-Shams The hadith of Jabir, which is in the two Sahihs, is presented, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Muadh: Why did you not pray, ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, by the sun and its brightness, and by the night when it covers you?’ In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Mujahid said, By the sun and its brightness, meaning its light. Qatadah said, By its brightness, means the entire day. Ibn Jarir said, "The correct way to say it is: God swears by the sun and its daytime, because the apparent light of the sun is the daytime. "By the moon when it follows it, Mujahid said, It follows it. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, By the moon when it follows it," meaning it follows the day. Qatadah said, "By the moon when it follows it," meaning it follows the night of the new moon, when the sun sets and the new moon is seen. Ibn Zayd said, "It follows it in the first half of the month, then it follows it, and it precedes it in the last half of the month. Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, By the moon when it follows it," meaning the Night of Decree. God, the Almighty, said, "By the day when it displays it, Mujahid said, It illuminates. Qatadah said, By the day when it displays it," meaning that the day covers it. Ibn Jarir said, "Some of the Arab scholars interpreted this to mean, 'By the day when it displays the darkness,' because the statement indicates this." I said If this speaker had interpreted it to mean and the day when it displays it, meaning the plain, it would have been more appropriate and his interpretation would have been correct in the words of God Almighty: and the night when it covers it, so it would have been better and stronger, and God knows best. For this reason, Mujahid said, and the day when it displays it, is like the words of God Almighty: and the day when it appears. As for Ibn Jarir, he preferred to have the pronoun in all of that refer to the sun because of its frequent mention. They said in the words of God Almighty: and the night when it covers it, meaning when it covers the sun when it sets and the horizons become dark. Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated on the authority of Safwan: Yazid ibn Dhi Hamama narrated to me: When night comes, the Lord, glory be to Him, says: My servants have been overwhelmed by My great creation. So the night is feared, while He who created it is more deserving of being feared. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. The statement of God, the Most High, {And the heaven and He who constructed it} may be that the word ma here is a source meaning and the heaven and its construction, which is the opinion of Qatadah. It may also be in the sense of who, meaning and the heaven and its Creator, which is the opinion of Mujahid. Both are interrelated, and construction means raising, like the statement of God, the Most High, {And the heaven We constructed with power, and indeed, We are expanding it. And the earth We spread out, so excellent are the spreaders.} Similarly, the statement of God, the Most High, {And the earth and He who spread it out,” Mujahid said: He spread it out, He spread it out. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And He who spread it out means He created in it. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He spread it out means He divided it. Mujahid, Qatada, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi, Al-Thawri, Abu Saleh, and Ibn Zayd said: Tahāha means to spread it out. This is the most famous of the sayings, and the majority of commentators agree with it. It is well-known among linguists. Al-Jawhari said: Tahāhutuhu is like Dahāhutuhu, meaning to spread it out. God the Almighty said: {And by the soul and He who proportioned it} meaning He created it well and upright in accordance with the correct fitrah, as God the Almighty said: {So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of God upon which He has created mankind. No change should there be in the creation of God.} And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Every child is born in a state of fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as an animal is born whole. Do you perceive any among them with their mutilated parts?” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] narrated from Abu Hurayrah. In Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Hammad al-Majashi’i, from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said: “God the Almighty says: ‘Indeed, I created My servants as upright ones, then the devils came to them and caused them to deviate from their religion.’” And God the Almighty said: {Then He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness.} meaning He guided it to its wickedness, that is, He made that clear to it and directed it to what was decreed for it. Ibn Abbas said, "And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness," meaning He showed it good and evil. This is what Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ath-Thawri said. Saeed ibn Jubayr said, "He inspired it with good and evil. Ibn Zayd said, He placed within it its wickedness and its righteousness. Ibn Jarir said, Ibn Bishr told us, Sufyan ibn Isa and Abu Asim An-Nabeel told us, they said, 'Uzra ibn Thabit told us, Yahya ibn Aqeel told me, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ya'mar, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad Ad-Dailami, who said, 'Imran ibn Husayn said to me, 'Do you think that what people do and strive for, is it something that has been decreed for them and has already passed them by as a predestination, or is it something that will come to them that their Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought them and the evidence was confirmed for them?' I said, 'Rather, it is something that has been decreed for them.' He said, 'Would that be injustice?'" He said: I was terrified by him. He said: I said to him, “There is nothing but that He created it and owns it. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.” He said: “May God guide you. I only asked you to inform your mind. A man from Muzaynah or Juhaynah came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘O Messenger of God, tell me what people do and strive for. Is it something that was decreed for them and passed them by from a predestination that had preceded them, or is it something that they will face that their Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought them and with which the proof was confirmed for them?’ He said: ‘Rather, it is something that has been decreed for them.’ He said: ‘Then what should we do?’ He said: ‘Whoever God created for one of the two stations, He prepares him for it.’ The confirmation of that is in the Book of God, the Most High: “And by the soul and He who proportioned it. And inspired it [with distinction] as to its wickedness and its righteousness.”’” Narrated by Ahmad and Muslim from the hadith of Uzrah ibn Thabit with this chain. And the Almighty’s saying: He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it. It is possible that the meaning is: He has succeeded who purifies his soul, that is, by obeying God, as Qatadah said: And purifies it from base morals and vices. Something similar is narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr. And like His Almighty’s saying: He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. “And he has failed who corrupts it,” that is, he corrupts it, that is, he neglects it and makes it weak by neglecting guidance until he commits sins and abandons the obedience of God Almighty. It is possible that the meaning is: He has succeeded who God purifies his soul, and he has failed who God corrupts his soul, as Al-Awfi and Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father and Abu Zur’ah told us: Sahl ibn Uthman told us, Abu Malik, meaning Amr ibn Hisham, told us on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: He says about the statement of God the Almighty: He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Successful is the soul that God the Almighty purifies. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Malik with it, and this Juwaybir is Ibn Sa’id, whose hadith is rejected, and Ad-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas. At-Tabarani said: Yahya bin Uthman bin Salih told us, my father told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by this verse: And by the soul and He who proportioned it * And inspired it with [what is] deviant and [what is] righteous, he would stop and then say: “O God, give my soul its righteousness. You are its Guardian and Master, and the best of those who purify it.” Another hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ya’qub ibn Hamid al-Madani told us, Abdullah al-Umawi told us, Ma’n ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari told us, on the authority of Hanzala ibn Ali al-Aslami, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite: ‘And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness.’ He said: ‘O God, give my soul its righteousness and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and Master.’ They did not include it from this chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Salih ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Aisha, that she missed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his bed, so she touched him with her hand and fell on him while he was prostrating and he was saying: ‘O God, give my soul its righteousness and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and Master.’ He is the only one who transmitted it.” Another Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Asim Al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “O God, I seek refuge in You from incapacity and laziness, old age, cowardice, miserliness, and the punishment of the grave. O God, grant my soul its piety and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and Master. O God, I seek refuge in You from a heart that does not fear You, and from a soul that is not satisfied, and from knowledge that is of no benefit, and a supplication that is not answered.” Zaid said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to teach them to us, and we will teach them to you. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith and Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, with this chain of transmission.

91:4: Mujahid said, By the sun and its brightness, meaning its light. Qatadah said, By its brightness, meaning the entire day. Ibn Jarir said, Its brightness, meaning the entire day. And the moon when it follows it, Mujahid said, It follows it. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, By the moon when it follows it, meaning it follows the day. Qatadah said, By the moon when it follows it, meaning it follows the night of the new moon, when the sun sets and the new moon is seen. Ibn Zayd said, It follows it in the first half of the month, then it follows it and it precedes it in the last half of the month. Malik said, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, By the moon when it follows it, meaning the Night of Decree. God, the Almighty, said, By the day when it displays it, Mujahid said, It illuminates. Qatadah said, By the day when it displays it, meaning it covers the day. Ibn Jarir said, Some of the Arab scholars interpreted this to mean, 'By the day when it displays the darkness,' because the statement indicates this. I said If this speaker had interpreted it to mean and the day when it displays it, meaning the plain, it would have been more appropriate and his interpretation would have been correct in the words of God Almighty: and the night when it covers it, so it would have been better and stronger, and God knows best. For this reason, Mujahid said, and the day when it displays it, is like the words of God Almighty: and the day when it appears. As for Ibn Jarir, he preferred to have the pronoun in all of that refer to the sun because of its frequent mention. They said in the words of God Almighty: and the night when it covers it, meaning when it covers the sun when it sets and the horizons become dark. Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated on the authority of Safwan: Yazid ibn Dhi Hamama narrated to me: When night comes, the Lord, glory be to Him, says: My servants have been overwhelmed by My great creation. So the night is feared, while He who created it is more deserving of being feared. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. The statement of God, the Most High, {And the heaven and He who constructed it} may be that the word ma here is a source meaning and the heaven and its construction, which is the opinion of Qatadah. It may also be in the sense of who, meaning and the heaven and its Creator, which is the opinion of Mujahid. Both are interrelated, and construction means raising, like the statement of God, the Most High, {And the heaven We constructed with power, and indeed, We are expanding it. And the earth We spread out, so excellent are the spreaders.} Similarly, the statement of God, the Most High, {And the earth and He who spread it out,” Mujahid said: He spread it out, He spread it out. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And He who spread it out means He created in it. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He spread it out means He divided it. Mujahid, Qatada, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi, Al-Thawri, Abu Saleh, and Ibn Zayd said: Tahāha means to spread it out. This is the most famous of the sayings, and the majority of commentators agree with it. It is well-known among linguists. Al-Jawhari said: Tahāhutuhu is like Dahāhutuhu, meaning to spread it out. God the Almighty said: {And by the soul and He who proportioned it} meaning He created it well and upright in accordance with the correct fitrah, as God the Almighty said: {So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of God upon which He has created mankind. No change should there be in the creation of God.} And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Every child is born in a state of fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as an animal is born whole. Do you perceive any among them with their mutilated parts?” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] narrated from Abu Hurayrah. In Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Hammad al-Majashi’i, from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said: “God the Almighty says: ‘Indeed, I created My servants as upright ones, then the devils came to them and caused them to deviate from their religion.’” And God the Almighty said: {Then He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness.} meaning He guided it to its wickedness, that is, He made that clear to it and directed it to what was decreed for it. Ibn Abbas said, And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness, meaning He showed it good and evil. This is what Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ath-Thawri said. Saeed ibn Jubayr said, He inspired it with good and evil. Ibn Zayd said, He placed within it its wickedness and its righteousness. Ibn Jarir said, "Ibn Bishr told us, Sufyan ibn Isa and Abu Asim An-Nabeel told us, they said, 'Uzra ibn Thabit told us, Yahya ibn Aqeel told me, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ya'mar, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad Ad-Dailami, who said, 'Imran ibn Husayn said to me, 'Do you think that what people do and strive for, is it something that has been decreed for them and has already passed them by as a predestination, or is it something that will come to them that their Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought them and the evidence was confirmed for them?' I said, 'Rather, it is something that has been decreed for them.' He said, 'Would that be injustice?'" He said: I was terrified by him. He said: I said to him, “There is nothing but that He created it and owns it. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.” He said: “May God guide you. I only asked you to inform your mind. A man from Muzaynah or Juhaynah came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘O Messenger of God, tell me what people do and strive for. Is it something that was decreed for them and passed them by from a predestination that had preceded them, or is it something that they will face that their Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought them and with which the proof was confirmed for them?’ He said: ‘Rather, it is something that has been decreed for them.’ He said: ‘Then what should we do?’ He said: ‘Whoever God created for one of the two stations, He prepares him for it.’ The confirmation of that is in the Book of God, the Most High: “And by the soul and He who proportioned it.
